answer: Treat admission as a journey, not a signup. A newcomer deposits refundable collateral in a time-locked escrow haven, then must complete a scored work voyage: several independently graded passing jobs attested by established peers whose recent endorsement neighborhoods barely overlap. Only when that path is on-ledger does the network open an admission vertex, still requiring K of those peers to co-sign. If a later clustering check shows the peers and the newcomer share one controller, the haven is slashed and those edges are burned, so a farm pays capital and lost-trust per head.
